title: Mammal ancestors were giving birth to live young 236 million years ago | New Scientist
description: Almost all mammals give birth rather than laying eggs, and we have new clues about when they began to do so
author: James Woodford

title: Running with a stroller seems to reduce the risk of injuries | New Scientist
description: Pushing a pram while running may reduce the force produced with each foot strike, decreasing the risk of injuries
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Live: Watch today's total solar eclipse | New Scientist
description: A total solar eclipse, Europe's first in 27 years, is set to be visible today. Watch it here
author: New Scientist

title: Mission to save NASA telescope back on track after loss of control | New Scientist
description: Katalyst’s LINK spacecraft might still be able to save NASA’s ailing Swift telescope from doom, despite a significant mishap
author: Jonathan O’Callaghan

title: Breast-augmentation method uses your own fat in dissolving scaffolds | New Scientist
description: A new approach to breast augmentation injects fat from elsewhere in the body into dissolvable scaffolds shaped like bra cups, which may lead to a more natural look and fewer complications
author: Alice Klein

title: Three black holes discovered in a young galaxy for the first time | New Scientist
description: Three massive black holes have been found in a galaxy that existed during the earliest times of the universe
author: James Woodford
